description:
Kivu EarthLab 

We are KIVU EarthLab, a team of young innovators from Bukavu, DRC, passionate about technology, AI, data science and environmental protection. Our mission is to use NASA Earth data to understand environmental changes and help protect communities. Join us to turn ideas into real-world solutions!
summary:
TerraPulse is a bilingual (FR/EN) environmental intelligence web platform developed by the Kivu EarthLab team to anticipate landslides and soil erosion in Bukavu (DRC).

Powered by an automated pipeline, the application leverages real NASA Earth observation data (precipitation and soil moisture via MERRA-2/POWER, vegetation index via MODIS, and SRTM radar topography). The platform features interactive time-series charts, a seasonal predictive model (3 to 12 months) with an 80% confidence interval, probabilistic risk diagnostics, and a vulnerability map comparing the communes of Kadutu, Ibanda, and Bagira.

Facing intense rainfall, deforestation, and Bukavu's steep topography, TerraPulse bridges the gap in local decision-support tools. By connecting "when to be vigilant" with "where to act first," this project is vital: it transforms complex spatial data into accessible preventive insights for policymakers, researchers, and local communities to protect lives and infrastructure.
details:
Comprehensive Project Description
  • Slogan: Listen to Earth. Understand Change. Predict Tomorrow.
  • Team: Kivu EarthLab (Bukavu, South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo)
  • Framework: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
  • Mission: Transforming NASA Earth observation data into actionable environmental intelligence to anticipate and prevent landslides and soil erosion in Bukavu.

1. Context & Problem Statement: Why Does Bukavu Need TerraPulse?

Located on the southern shore of Lake Kivu at an altitude of approximately 1,500 meters, the city of Bukavu faces acute hydro-geomorphological hazards due to three compounding factors:

  1. Steep Topography: The city is built across a series of hills with steep slopes (frequently exceeding 15° to 25°) composed of weathered volcanic and clayey soils.
  2. Intense Rainfall Pressure: The highland tropical climate generates heavy rainy seasons that rapidly saturate the ground, increasing soil weight and reducing internal shear strength.
  3. Rapid Urbanization & Vegetation Loss: Deforestation on hillsides and unregulated construction on fragile slopes strip away the root networks that mechanically stabilize the soil.

The Core Problem: Although NASA satellites continuously monitor the atmosphere, soil moisture, and vegetation cover over this region, these datasets remain raw, complex, scattered, and inaccessible to local authorities, urban planners, and residents. TerraPulse bridges this gap by translating space-based observations into a clear, actionable decision-support tool.

2. Scientific Positioning: Seasonal Prevention vs. Real-Time Emergency Alerts

A core strength of TerraPulse lies in its scientific honesty. Earth observation satellite products involve specific processing latencies and spatial resolutions. Therefore, TerraPulse does not claim to replace a minute-by-minute emergency weather siren; instead, it operates as a seasonal prevention and territorial planning tool.

It answers two complementary questions:

  • "When should we be vigilant?" (Anticipating high-risk quarters and months ahead).
  • "Where should we act first?" (Pinpointing the most vulnerable hillsides and communes).

3. NASA Data Architecture (The Scientific Backbone)

TerraPulse relies on an automated Python pipeline (telecharger_donnees_nasa.py, built strictly with standard Python libraries and intelligent local caching) that extracts real quantitative data covering 2021–2025 around Bukavu (lat: -2.51, lon: 28.85) from four authoritative NASA sources:

  1. Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR) — NASA POWER / MERRA-2 Reanalysis:
    • Nature: Bias-corrected daily precipitation totals (~50 km grid).
    • Role: Quantifies water input driving surface runoff and soil infiltration.
    • Nature: Surface soil saturation rate (ranging from 0 to 1).
    • Role: A primary indicator of slope mechanical instability—as soil nears saturation, the risk of slope failure and landslides increases sharply.
    • Nature: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index captured every 16 days at a 250-meter spatial resolution.
    • Custom Processing: The script automatically filters out cloud-contaminated pixels (using the product's pixel reliability band) and masks out Lake Kivu waters (median NDVI < 0.10) to isolate terrestrial land surfaces.
    • Nature: Radar Digital Elevation Model at 30-meter resolution (1 arc-second).
    • Role: Enables precise calculation of slope inclination across every hillside in the city.

4. The Four Functional Pillars of the Web Application

The web interface , fully bilingual (English / French), self-contained, and deployable without heavy backend infrastructure, is structured around four core pillars:

Pillar 1: DETECT (Data Acquisition & Transparency)

  • Centralizes the 2021–2025 multi-sensor historical dataset into a lightweight, ready-to-use module.
  • Allows researchers to upload their own custom CSV time-series datasets to test alternative timeframes or regions.

Pillar 2: ANALYZE (Multi-Scale Visualization & Dynamic Interpretation)

  • Displays three synchronized time-series charts (Precipitation, Soil Moisture, NDVI) with dynamic temporal aggregation: daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
    1. Curve Reading: Mean, extremes, threshold exceedance counts, and underlying statistical trends.
    2. Environmental Impact for Kivu: Physical translation of these metrics into local runoff, soil saturation, and root cohesion dynamics.

Pillar 3: PREDICT (Seasonal Modeling & Probabilistic Risk Diagnostics)

  • Learning Algorithm: A least-squares statistical model trains on the selected historical window (requiring at least 24 full months for statistical robustness) to extract the typical seasonal cycle for each calendar month alongside any linear long-term trend (retained only if statistically significant beyond twice its standard error).
    • Landslide Risk: Combines the probability of heavy rainfall (> 150 mm/month) and critical soil saturation (calibrated to the 80th percentile of MERRA-2 observations, and customizable by the user).
    • Soil Erosion Risk: Combines heavy rainfall probability with vegetation cover degradation (NDVI < 0.40).
    • Each forecasted month is classified as Normal, Vigilance, or High Risk.

Pillar 4: LOCATE (Spatial Mapping of Vulnerable Hillsides)

  • The 10 km × 10 km urban and peri-urban area of Bukavu is partitioned into 1,433 terrestrial grid cells (231 meters each).
  • For every cell, TerraPulse computes a composite Vulnerability Index (0 to 1):
    Index = Slope Score x (0.5 + 0.5 x Vegetation Deficit)
    (A steep 25° slope with dense forest cover scores a moderate 0.5, whereas the same slope stripped of vegetation reaches the critical score of 1.0).

5. Dual Impact: Local Communities & Scientific Research

  • For Local Communities, Civil Protection & Policymakers: Intuitive dual basemaps (Esri Street Map and Satellite Imagery) allow stakeholders to anticipate high-risk seasons—enabling proactive drainage clearing, construction restrictions on critical slopes, and targeted reforestation campaigns in Ibanda and Kadutu.
  • For the Scientific Community: A reproducible workflow enabling one-click export of filtered time series, forecasts, 80% confidence bounds, and full NASA data citations in CSV and JSON formats.

6. Future Roadmap

  1. Direct NASA SMAP Integration: Upgrading from 50 km MERRA-2 reanalysis soil wetness to high-resolution radar/radiometer soil moisture measurements from the NASA SMAP mission (via NASA Earthdata authentication).
  2. Expanded Linguistic Accessibility: Adding Swahili (the primary local language spoken across Bukavu) alongside English and French to maximize community adoption.
  3. Regional Scaling: Extending the exact same automated pipeline to other hazard-prone cities across the East African Rift (such as Goma, Uvira, and Kigali).
